parameters.description:
The query parameter is used to search text-based fields for records that match specific query terms. The query can be multiple words or numbers. Every record that matches the beginning of any word or number in the query string is returned.

Fuzzy search is supported for the following text-based field types: Text fields, Multi Line Text fields, and RegExp fields.

For example, you might want to search for records related to Tesla vehicles: `query=Tesla`. In this example the API would return every record for the given custom object where any of the supported text fields contain the word 'Tesla'.

You can include multiple words or numbers in your search. For example: `query=Tesla Honda 2020`. This search phrase would be URL encoded as `query=Tesla%20Honda%202020` and return every record for the custom object for which any of the supported text fields contained 'Tesla', 'Honda', or '2020'.

parameters.name: brand_id
parameters.description:
When brand separation is enabled, scopes user results to the specified brand.
This parameter applies only when the account has brand separation enabled
(`brand_user_separation_eap`). Non-user document types are unaffected.

Accepted values:

* "all" — apply no brand scoping.
* 0 — return only account-scoped (brand-less) end users; all agents and admins remain visible.
* A numeric brand id — if the brand has user separation enabled, return that
  brand's end users plus the agents with membership in that brand and all admins.
  If the brand does not have user separation enabled, the request falls back to
  account scope (0). A brand id that does not exist on the account matches no users.

Any other value returns 400 Bad Request, whether or not brand separation is enabled.

The query keyword form (`query=type:user brand_id:{brand_id}`) continues to work. It
matches the brand id as indexed on every document type, so admins match only through
their brand memberships, and it does not apply the account-scope fallback for brands
without user separation.

has brand separation enabled (`brand_user_separation_eap`); ignored
otherwise so existing numeric callers continue to behave as before.

* Any other non-numeric string.

  globally unique so brand scoping is meaningless).

When `external_ids` is provided without `brand_id`, the request defaults
to account scope (`0`).

is always passed as an Integer (`0` for account scope; the brand id
otherwise) for backward compatibility with existing job consumers.
